findings.finding: Oracle's own reported interest bill contradicts the base EPS path, and that path sets every company_path price. Base FY2028 interest is $2.04B (val.result.scenarios[base].forecast[1].interest, opening debt $12.58B). Oracle reported $1.428B of interest in Q1 FY2027 alone (rp_f_int_q1fy27, about $5.7B a year on $125B of notes). As a result, base FY2028 GAAP EPS after SBC is $10.94 (company_path.fiscal_years.base[1]). That is ABOVE management's own non-GAAP FY2028 target of $10.65 (rp_g_fy28_eps_fam), which excludes SBC and amortization. The base profit path is more optimistic than the company's guidance, and that comes from the missing-debt defect, not from evidence.
findings.where: casefile.json company_path.fiscal_years.base / scenarios.*.rows; val.result.scenarios[1].forecast[0..4].interest; evidence rp_f_int_q1fy27, rp_g_fy28_eps_fam
findings.fix: Add 'longtermnotesandloans' to facts.INSTANT_TAGS['long_term_debt'] and rerun ticker-value. Then check that base FY2028 GAAP EPS sits below the $10.65 non-GAAP target, and that FY2029/FY2030 EPS ($13.86/$16.84 now) are read against $16/$21 (rp_g_fy29_eps_fam, rp_g_fy30_eps_fam). Explain each gap (SBC, amortization, interest) in the base reason.

findings.finding: The near-term capex in the base contradicts Oracle's own reported run rate, which flatters FCF and the funding need. The base stub (2026-10-29 to 2027-05-31, about 7 months) carries $32.8B of capex ($6.27B maintenance + $26.53B growth), about $4.7B a month. Oracle spent $28.5B in Q1 FY2027 alone (rp_f_capex_q1fy27, about $9.5B a month). FY2026 capex also came in 11% above the last guide ($55.7B vs about $50B). The implied FY2027 total is about $80B, below the $90-95B guide in the press summary and far below the Q1 run rate. The engine's own flag val.capex_below_history (planned 34.6% of revenue vs 82.6% history) says the same, but it is left 'not_priced'.
findings.where: casefile.json val.case.scenarios[1].periods[0] (growth_capex, maintenance_capex); fc.anchors.reinvestment_identity.base; risk register val.capex_below_history; position.json drivers.sales_to_capital
findings.fix: Anchor the FY2027 stub capex on the citable Q1 FY2027 actual and the capex track record (rp_f_capex_q1fy27, rp_f_capex_fy26 vs the guide), e.g. a capex/funding override for year 0. Otherwise state in the base reason why spending halves after Q1. Price val.capex_below_history in the bear path or as a quantified adjustment.

findings.finding: The base adopts management's multi-year targets ($130B FY2028, $185B FY2029, $225B FY2030, from the 2025-10-16 FAM) without reading them against a long-range track record. The only track record checked is three distinct short-dated periods (FY2026, Q4 FY2026, Q1 FY2027), ratio 1.008. Several of the company's own misses were not used to adjust or bound the multi-year path: the FY2026 'over 40%' cloud growth landed at 39%, and capex overran its guides in sequence ($35B, then $50B, then $55.7B actual). Prior long-range targets were not retrieved, e.g. the 2023 analyst-meeting FY2026 target against the FY2026 actual of $67.4B. The core reason itself says the binding limit is capacity delivery, where the company over-runs, yet it applies no adjustment. The 2026-10-28 Investor Day 8-K (not citable until 2026-10-30) may have changed these targets.
findings.where: position.json drivers.growth_anchor (base, adjust_by_track_record=false) and drivers.growth_half_life (base override_4); gather/reports.json guidance_track
findings.fix: Retrieve the previous long-range target and its outcome (the 2023 FAM FY2026 target vs the FY2026 10-K actual) and add it to guidance_track. Show the base explicitly as 'management target, unadjusted' with the capex-delivery overrun as a quantified bear lever, or haircut the delivery timing. Rerun with as_of on or after 2026-10-30 to use the updated Investor Day targets.

findings.finding: The bear growth anchor is tiered 'contracted', but its size rests on press attribution only. The ~$300B OpenAI contract and its 'about half of RPO' come from un_digitimes_openai_20250911 and un_barchart_20260220 (syndicated, the WSJ original was not read). The issuer discloses neither, and its 10-K shows no customer with 10% or more of revenue (ex_k_cust_ge10pct_fy26). The '$27B of the $73B FY2028 OCI target' is the analyst's own arithmetic. Labelling it 'contracted' presents a hypothesis as contract evidence.
findings.where: casefile.json fc.driver_sources (growth_anchor, bear, tier contracted); fc.overrides override_1; position.json drivers.growth_anchor.source_tier.bear
findings.fix: Retier the bear growth anchor as an analyst hypothesis (press-attributed concentration), keep the RPO maturity split as the only contracted part, and say in the bear reason that the concentration size is unconfirmed by Oracle.

findings.finding: The tiers on two levers hide engine rules. growth_half_life for bear and bull is tiered 'guidance' while its default_class is CONST: it is the engine's 0.8x/1.3x spread, not company data. driver_gaps does list it, so the table row is correct. tax_rate is tiered 'own_history', yet the engine normalized the 12.0% effective rate to 15% by rule (warning tax_normalized), and it is missing from the table's 'assumptions without company data' row even though core gaps say tax_rate stays on the engine rule.
findings.where: casefile.json fc.driver_sources (growth_half_life bear/bull, tax_rate); fc.warnings tax_normalized; fc.driver_gaps; out/table_he.md row 'הנחות בלי נתון של החברה'
findings.fix: Tier growth_half_life bear/bull as default. Either supply an evidenced normalized tax rate (FY2024-FY2025 effective rates ex the Ampere gain) or add tax_rate to driver_gaps so the table row shows it.

findings.finding: The multiple check against named competitors is missing, and the own-history multiple basis is not comparable. company_path forward P/E (base 12.1x, bull 32.2x at year 0) is compared only with own_history TRAILING GAAP P/E (15.4/37.4/64.8, 2021-11 to 2026-10). That series mixes bases (trailing vs forward), includes the one-time Ampere gain and covers the AI re-rating. No forward P/E of MSFT, AMZN or GOOGL (the IaaS rivals named in the 10-K) appears, because the FMP quote was denied, and no fallback was tried. The bull is not at a peak multiple (32x vs a 64.8x high), but 'comparable stage' cannot be checked.
findings.where: casefile.json company_path.own_history; position.json gaps 'path: No forward P/E of the named competitors'
findings.fix: Make one bounded Alpha Vantage COMPANY_OVERVIEW probe each (ForwardPE) for MSFT, AMZN and GOOGL, record why each competes (IaaS rival per the 10-K), and add them as context rows. Label own_history as trailing GAAP ex the Ampere gain where possible.

findings.finding: The ROIC behind the company_path multiple differs from the ROIC behind the DCF value in every scenario: path 6% / 11% / 16% vs terminal_roic 9% / 13% / 17%. The base 11% is a midpoint chosen between two own-history figures (6.4% marginal, 12.8-14.8% total), so it is analyst judgement, not an own-history number. The bull reason also says the margin approaches 'AWS and Google Cloud', but its evidence_ids hold no competitor source (fd_aws_q2_2026 / fd_gcloud_q2_2026 exist in field).
findings.where: casefile.json company_path.scenarios.{bear,base,bull}.roic and reason_he; position.json drivers.terminal_roic; position/path.json
findings.fix: Use one ROIC per scenario in both places, or state why the path ROIC differs. Tier the base 11% as an analyst choice. Either cite fd_aws_q2_2026 / fd_gcloud_q2_2026 as competitor context in the bull reason, or drop the competitor comparison.

findings.finding: The revenue track-record count is overstated. core cites 'ratio 1.008 over 6 periods', but gather/numbers.json notes that ticker-check counted the same three periods twice (numbers and reports lanes): there are 3 distinct periods, 3 beats and 0 misses.
findings.fix: Deduplicate guidance_track in the merge and restate the reason as '1.008 over 3 distinct periods'.
